maria-ruiz: Quick heads-up — after the continuous-batching heuristic change (deployed ~09:12 UTC, PR #2345) we're seeing 95p latency spikes on prod-runtime-1. P50 looks fine but 95/99 are up ~6-8x. Rolling 5% traffic to the new heuristic when spikes started.

jonathan-lee: Dashboard -> https://dash.redwood.local/r/xyz. 95p jumped from ~120ms to ~870ms around 09:13. Throughput dropped ~18% concurrently. Any traces or logs?

maria-ruiz: Quick profiler snippet from the runtime node (trimmed):

```
KVCache: hit 73.1% miss 26.9%
batcher: avg_batch_tokens=12 avg_batch_size=3
continuous_batching: token_budget_target=0  <-- suspicious
kernel_selector: selected=matmul-slow fallback_count=8
rpc_latency: tail=0.87s
```

kai_wu: Interesting — token_budget_target=0 stands out. That would cause the batcher to avoid forming larger batches and trigger many small immediate batches, increasing per-token overhead and changing kernel selection patterns. Did the PR change rounding or integer math?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Deployed runtime-service @ commit abcdef123 by @maria-ruiz at 1759456100. Canary traffic=5%.

sre-oncall: Noted surge on prod-runtime-1 and prod-runtime-2. I'm seeing queue-depth oscillation in logs (lots of tiny batches, then occasional big batches). Could be head-of-line blocking from a prefer_short_requests queue policy.

maria-ruiz: Repro steps on staging that show the behavior:
```
# start dev pool with heuristic flag overrides
./run_runtime --flags continuous_batching.token_budget_target=0 --flags queue_policy=prefer_short_requests
wrk -t4 -c200 --script ./scripts/prompt_stream.lua http://staging-runtime:8080/generate
# observe p95 jump and throughput drop in ~30s
```
When I force token_budget_target=64 and queue_policy=fair, p95 stabilizes and throughput returns to expected.

jonathan-lee: Please enable kernel selector trace logging and grab pprof for the affected pods for 5m. Also open a rollback toggle for the heuristic (10% -> 0% for canary) while we triage.

kai_wu: Quick hypothesis: two bugs combined — 1) integer division truncation in token budget calc leads to 0 for short-request-heavy workloads; 2) prefer_short_requests causes many tiny batches that change seq_len distribution, and kernel_selector has a mem-plan heuristic that incorrectly falls back to a slower kernel for those mixed batches. I'll prepare a small patch to (a) fix division -> ceil, (b) short-circuit the mem-plan fallback when batch_size < 8.

maria-ruiz: Action items:
- rolling heuristic back on canary (10%->0%) now (maria)
- collect pprof + kernel logs from affected pods (jonathan)
- patch PR for integer/ceil fix + unit tests (kai)
- postmortem draft after rollback and traces are collected (maria)

maria-ruiz: Thanks all — I'll update when rollback completes. :thumbsup:
